title: Why Buffett and Munger's Third Partner Vanished from the Billionaire List
alt_title_1: Rick Guerin's $40 Berkshire Margin Call in the 1973-1974 Crash
alt_title_2: Being Smart and In a Hurry: Warren Buffett's Ultimate Leverage Warning
description_hook: Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger originally invested alongside a brilliant third partner named Rick Guerin. During the 1973-1974 market crash (~70% drop), Guerin was leveraged on margin loans and forced to sell his Berkshire Hathaway shares to Buffett for under $40 apiece.

scenes.headline: Buffett and Munger Originally Had a Third Partner
scenes.stat_label: PRICE RICK GUERIN SOLD BERKSHIRE STOCK IN 1974
bullets: Invested side by side with Buffett & Munger in the 1960s-70s
Forced out just before decades of historic compounding
scenes.narration: Everyone studies Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger, yet almost nobody remembers their brilliant third investing partner, Rick Guerin, who sold his Berkshire Hathaway shares for under forty dollars apiece.
scenes.source: Warren Buffett interview recounted by Mohnish Pabrai (2013)

scenes.headline: Margin Loans Met the 1973-1974 70% Bear Crash
bullets: Guerin borrowed margin debt to accelerate his returns
Lenders forced him to sell Berkshire shares to Buffett under $40
scenes.narration: During the brutal 1973 and 1974 market crash, when stocks plunged roughly seventy percent, Guerin held margin loans and got hit with margin calls, forcing him to sell his Berkshire stock to Buffett under forty dollars.
scenes.source: Warren Buffett interview recounted by Mohnish Pabrai (2013)

scenes.headline: Equally Smart, Only Impatient With Borrowed Debt
scenes.left_body: Margin debt + 1974 slump -> forced exit at <$40/share
scenes.right_body: Zero margin calls -> held through storm -> $600,000+/share
scenes.narration: Years later, Buffett told investor Mohnish Pabrai why Rick disappeared from the billionaire ranks: Charlie and Warren knew they would grow wealthy eventually, whereas equally smart Rick was in a hurry.
scenes.source: Warren Buffett interview recounted by Mohnish Pabrai (2013)

scenes.headline: Never Carry Callable Debt Into a Multi-Year Slump
scenes.stat_label: UNINTERRUPTED STAYING POWER BEATS LEVERAGED SPEED
scenes.stat_subtext: 0% brokerage margin + 12-month cash buffer -> zero forced sales
scenes.narration: Ban callable margin debt from your core portfolio and hold twelve months of living cash in reserve, ensuring no bear market ever forces you to liquidate decades of future compounding.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin protocol (advice, not a study)

scenes.headline: You Only Need to Get Rich Once
scenes.stat_label: NEVER RISK PERMANENT CAPITAL TO ARRIVE TWO YEARS EARLY
bullets: Patience survives every 50% to 70% historical drawdown
Leverage hands strangers the right to sell your bottom
scenes.narration: You only have to get rich once, so never gamble permanent survival just to cross the finish line two years early.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule based on Buffett & Pabrai (2013)
